title: Pea and Mint Risotto
subtitle: Fresh spring risotto with peas, mint, and Parmesan
excerpt: A bright, fresh risotto made with Arborio rice, sweet peas, and handfuls of mint, finished with butter and Parmesan. Light enough for a spring main course.

recipe.sourceNotes: This is a spring and summer variation on the classic Italian risotto technique, using the freshness of peas and mint to create a lighter result than the mushroom version. In Italy, risi e bisi (rice and peas) is a Venetian dish made for the feast of St Mark on 25 April, when the first peas of the year arrived in Venice by boat from the mainland. It is looser than a conventional risotto, almost a thick soup, and was historically served to the Doge of Venice. This version is firmer and more conventional, with mint added for brightness. Frozen peas work extremely well and are often sweeter and more tender than fresh shelled peas, which can be starchy if not absolutely fresh.

content.text: Add the peas in the last 5 minutes of cooking so they retain their bright green colour and do not turn khaki. Adding a handful of mint leaves at the very end, off the heat, preserves the fresh, herbal flavour that would be lost if cooked through. The risotto should be loose and flowing when it goes into the bowls: it will thicken on the plate.

Keep the stock hot in a separate pan. Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Fry the onion for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the rice and stir to coat for 2 minutes. Add the wine and stir until absorbed.
Add the hot stock a ladleful at a time, stirring frequently, waiting until almost absorbed before adding more. Continue for 18 to 20 minutes until the rice is tender with a slight bite.

Add the peas for the last 5 minutes of cooking. Remove from the heat. Beat in the cold butter, Parmesan, and lemon juice. Roughly tear in the mint leaves. Season with salt and pepper. Cover and rest for 2 minutes. Serve immediately, flowing in the bowl.
